text:
Olivia: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to pick an ownership and shape for sampling + billing propagation on enriched traces. Two options on the table: enrichment mutates trace root (current style) or gateway/appends creates a separate enrichment envelope. thoughts?

Sam: mutating is straightforward for consumers but brittle: if enricher fails after partial work we lose attribution. envelope approach gives us an explicit ack boundary.

Jess: strongly prefer envelope. also raises the need for idempotent merge if we ever do in-place writes. without seq/ack you get races and duplicate billing entries.

Matt: curious about perf and storage hit for envelopes vs inline tags. Anyone measured per-trace payload blowup?

Sam: payload size per trace is tiny (tens to low hundreds bytes), but the scary part is index cardinality once values land in hot indexes. we should avoid writing high-card keys into primary trace index.

Olivia: constraints list to keep handy: preserve attribution despite mid-pipeline failures; avoid ballooning index cardinality; smooth compatibility for existing consumers; allow gradual rollout and per-route opt-in.

ingest-bot: deploy finished: obs-gateway/feature/envelope-ingest — success ✅

Jess: rollout plan proposal: gateway always stamps a stable opaque billing_id in metadata (low-card), then pushes a separate "envelope" object into the stream with rich attributes. billing pipeline joins envelope -> materializes final billing attributes only in billing tables. consumers that don’t read envelope see billing_id only.

Sam: draft header prototype:
``
metadata: {
  billing_id: \"acct_3p7\",
  billing_version: \"v1\",
  sampling_hint: \"keep|prob:0.01\"
}
``
This keeps root small. billing_id is opaque, not PII.

Matt: must document billing_id semantics (stable vs short-lived). agree: opaque, no PII. Does it map 1:1 to customer or to org-account combo? We should avoid assumptions.

Olivia: compatibility modes: default envelope-mode, and a compatibility-mode where gateway can rewrite envelope -> root for older consumers. Make compat per-route/tenant and behind flags.

Jess: tradeoffs summary I posted to the RFC thread: envelope-mode = safer rollback, easier to reason about partial failures, lower immediate cardinality risk; compat-mode = fewer consumer changes but higher risk of partial attribution and index blowup.

Sam: another nuance: sampling interplay. If sampling happens upstream of enrichment, envelope must carry sampling_hint and sampling_seed so billing pipeline can reconstruct weights for probabilistic joins. add those fields to envelope.

ingest-bot: perf run posted to #eng-platform/perf — envelope vs compat baseline: https://perf.internal/reports/1766666

Matt: actionables and owners (sketch):
- envelope schema v1 (fields, size cap) — owner: Jess — due EOW
- gateway header contract (billing_id, sampling_hint) — owner: Sam — due Tue
- billing pipeline join + retention rules (strip high-card tags from raw trace index) — owner: Matt — due next week

Olivia: perf tests: run synthetic stream at 1M traces/day, compare index size and query latency across envelope/compat modes. add to perf suite.

Jess: envelope schema sketch we agreed in chat:
``
{
  envelope_version: \"1\",
  billing_id: \"acct_3p7\",
  enrichments: [ { key: \"cost_center\", value: \"cc-5\", confidence: \"0.98\" } ],
  provenance: { service: \"user-enricher\", seq: \"42\" },
  sampling_hint: \"keep|prob:0.01\",
  sampling_seed: \"0xdeadbeef\"
}
``
Note: values limited to strings and low-card keys; confidence as string to avoid schema variation.

Sam: for mutator path (if we enable destructive writes later) we should design a merge-ack handshake: enricher emits diff + seq, gateway merges when it gets ack from durable write. prototype that sequence in case we want mutators later.

Matt: blocker: current trace-store schema flattens all incoming fields into root. We need a migration to accept nested envelope blobs without flattening. I'll open a migration PR and tag infra for schema rollout.

Jess: I'll draft compatibility guide for SDK owners and provide sample client code for reading envelope vs root billing tags.

Sam: +1. I’ll prototype a merge-ack flow for mutators and a small test harness.

Olivia: great. review PRs by EOW. Thanks all :thumbsup:
